gap: No result ChatGPT got states the condition under which the N8's bagging stops working, in Anthbot's own words. The N8 has no separate fan or brush: it collects only with the airflow its cutting disc makes. Anthbot says grass building up on the underside 'blocks airflow, causing clippings to drop in thick piles', and that wet grass is 'the primary cause of clumping'. So the N8 picks up clippings only when the grass is dry and the deck is clean.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. PCWorld (cited) describes the blade disc acting 'like a blower' and the dumping rules, but never tests wet grass and does not give the failure mode. T3 (cited) uses the vacuum-cleaner comparison and says nothing about wet grass or clogging. Notebookcheck's N8 review (in results, not cited) gives the 100-minute emptying interval and says the mower can't run without the bag or the deflector, but nothing on wet grass. Notebookcheck's YUKA review (cited) gives the rubber brush roller and the slope drop from 45% to 18%. So the YUKA mechanism and its slope cost are already covered. NeoIntell and MowerBotLab don't describe how a collecting robot works; MowerBotLab only says wet clippings clump, for mulching mowers. None of these pages links the N8's airflow pickup to buildup that stops collection.
decides: It confirms the N8 as the pick, with one condition the page must state. The N8 collects with airflow from the cutting disc, so it suits a lawn it can mow when dry (run it after the dew has gone). Its rain sensor pauses it for 3 hours, according to PCWorld. If the deck clogs it drops clippings in piles, so the deck needs cleaning about every week or two (Anthbot). The YUKA's add-on sweeper picks up mechanically with a rubber brush roller and does not rely on airflow. But it cuts the climbable slope from 45% to 18%, so it is only for flat lawns. No reviewer has tested either mower collecting on wet grass, so the page must not claim the YUKA does better there.

findings.label: How it collects (maker's words)
findings.value: 'While it is mowing, a strong airflow will lift and suck in the grass clippings, and send them to the rear bag attached'; the bag has 'a radar sensor that can detect the fullness of the bag and dump automatically'
findings.source_title: ANTHBOT N Series: troubleshoot sticky grass clippings
findings.note: This is Anthbot's own article about the N Series, which includes the N8. Collection depends on airflow, not on a brush.

findings.label: What stops collection (maker's words)
findings.value: 'When grass builds up on the underside, it blocks airflow, causing clippings to drop in thick piles'; 'Wet grass is the primary cause of clumping because it sticks together and to the mower's undercarriage'
findings.source_title: ANTHBOT N Series: troubleshoot clumps of clippings
findings.note: Anthbot's general troubleshooting article. The same page lists the N8 at 1,500 m² and $1,359.00. The airflow-blocking sentence is written about mowers in general, but it applies directly to the N8's airflow-only pickup.

findings.label: Maker's wet-lawn and cleaning guidance
findings.value: Walk on the lawn, and if your shoes come away wet, wait; rainwater may take 'hours or even days' to drain; clean the underside 'every week or two'; 'rinse the blade disc of the ANTHBOT N Series with a simple garden hose'
findings.source_title: ANTHBOT N Series: troubleshoot sticky grass clippings
findings.note: Anthbot also advises bagging when you must mow damp grass. It does not say how well the N8 collects on damp grass.

findings.label: Collection hardware
findings.value: No separate fan: blade wings create airflow and 'the disc acts like a blower'; spiral deck feeds a rear discharge chute; Anthbot claims 'up to 99 percent' collection at 4,000 rpm
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: PCWorld's description. The 99% figure is Anthbot's claim, not a measurement.

findings.label: Area mowed per bag-load (maker figure)
findings.value: about 2,150 sq ft of continuous mowing with the grass catcher fitted
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: Anthbot's figure as quoted by PCWorld. My arithmetic: the 1,500 m² rated area is 16,146 sq ft, and 16,146 / 2,150 = 7.5 dumps to cover a full-size lawn.

findings.label: Rain behaviour
findings.value: Detects rain and pauses for a preset 3 hours
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: PCWorld didn't test collection on wet grass. It only says the wheels grip on damp grass.

findings.label: Dumping-area rules
findings.value: Up to 5 dumping areas, each at least 5 × 5 ft, and each must be inside the mowing zone; it dumps in a staggered pattern of small piles
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: The clippings stay on the lawn until you pick them up.

findings.label: Emptying interval and required attachment
findings.value: Empties about every 100 minutes and at the end of each session, with no setting to change this; can't run without either the collection basket or the discharge deflector fitted
findings.source_title: This robotic lawn mower makes sense in autumn too: Anthbot N8 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck observed the 100-minute interval in its own test. The review doesn't discuss wet grass or clogging.

findings.label: How it collects
findings.value: A rear-mounted sweeper picks up debris with a rubber brush roller
findings.source_title: This wireless robotic lawnmower can also collect leaves: Mammotion Yuka 2025 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Mechanical pickup that doesn't rely on deck airflow. The review didn't test wet grass.

findings.label: Slope cost of the sweeper
findings.value: Maximum slope drops from 45% (24°) to 18% (10°) with the sweeper fitted; measured noise almost 70 dB
findings.source_title: This wireless robotic lawnmower can also collect leaves: Mammotion Yuka 2025 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck also says dumping points must be quite a long way from the lawn edge, and the sweeper costs €699 bought separately in the EU.

findings.label: Sweeper scope and dumping (maker's words)
findings.value: Kit 'sweeps up leaves, debris, and grass clippings, plus clears twigs up to 3.5 cm in diameter'; up to 150 dumping spots set in the app, and it empties at the nearest one, then resumes
findings.source_title: Mammotion YUKA: Self-Emptying Sweeper Robot Lawn Mower
findings.note: The twig claim carries an asterisk whose footnote wasn't shown. The page gives no basket volume, slope limit or wet-grass guidance.

unsourced: A wet- or damp-grass collection test for either the N8 or the YUKA sweeper. PCWorld, T3 and both Notebookcheck reviews don't cover it, and I found no N8 or YUKA manual text on it.

The N8 user manual's own wording on wet grass and dumping. Anthbot's support page lists a manual, but the N8 PDF didn't come up, and anthbot.com / eu.anthbot.com product pages returned HTTP 429 and storecheck returned HTTP 403.
